definition: An important point or stage in a project.
exampleSentence: Finishing the first version of the app was a big milestone for the team.

definition: A product or result that must be handed over in a project.
exampleSentence: The main deliverable for this month is a working payment page.

definition: A plan that shows when each part of a project will happen.
exampleSentence: The client asked for a realistic timeline before signing the contract.

definition: A long-term plan that shows future goals and steps.
exampleSentence: Our product roadmap includes a mobile app and a new dashboard next year.

definition: The amount of work a person or team has to do.
exampleSentence: My workload is very heavy this week because two colleagues are sick.

definition: The process of helping new employees start their job.
exampleSentence: Good onboarding helps new employees feel welcome and productive quickly.

definition: A short description of a feature from the user's point of view.
exampleSentence: Each user story describes what the customer wants and why.

definition: A meeting where a team discusses what went well and what to improve.
exampleSentence: At the sprint retrospective, the team agreed to write more tests.

definition: A short daily meeting where each person shares progress and problems.
exampleSentence: Our stand-up meeting starts at nine thirty every morning.

definition: An early model of a product used for testing ideas.
exampleSentence: The designers built a simple prototype to test the idea with users.

definition: A simple drawing that shows the layout of a screen.
exampleSentence: The designer shared a wireframe of the new home page with the team.

definition: A realistic picture of how a screen or product will look.
exampleSentence: The client approved the mockup, so the developers can start coding.

definition: Passing a problem to a more senior person or team.
exampleSentence: The customer asked for an escalation because the problem was not fixed.

definition: A temporary way to avoid a problem until it is fixed.
exampleSentence: Until the bug is fixed, the workaround is to restart the app.

definition: The main reason why a problem happened.
exampleSentence: The team spent two days finding the root cause of the outage.

definition: A quick update that fixes a serious problem in live software.
exampleSentence: We released a hotfix the same evening to stop the payment errors.

definition: Returning a system to an earlier working version.
exampleSentence: After the failed update, the team performed a rollback to the previous version.

definition: A list of changes made in each version of software.
exampleSentence: Read the changelog to see which bugs were fixed in this version.

definition: The limits of what a project will and will not include.
exampleSentence: Adding a chat feature is outside the agreed project scope.

definition: A short report about the current progress of work.
exampleSentence: Please send a short status update to the client every Friday.

definition: A task that someone must do after a meeting.
exampleSentence: Each action item from the meeting has an owner and a deadline.

definition: The amount of work a person, team or system can handle.
exampleSentence: The team has no capacity for new projects until next month.

definition: To give money, time or people for a particular purpose.
exampleSentence: The company will allocate more budget to cybersecurity next year.

definition: To complete the last details of something.
exampleSentence: We need to finalize the contract before the end of the week.

definition: To make a process simpler and more efficient.
exampleSentence: The new software will streamline the way we handle invoices.

definition: To pass a problem to someone with more authority.
exampleSentence: If the issue is not solved today, please escalate it to the manager.

definition: To make plans or ideas agree with each other.
exampleSentence: We must align our goals with the company strategy.

definition: To share many ideas quickly in a group.
exampleSentence: Let us brainstorm some names for the new product.

definition: To pay another company to do part of your work.
exampleSentence: Many companies outsource their customer support to other countries.

definition: To make a process work by itself, without people.
exampleSentence: We want to automate the testing process to save time.

definition: A standard used to compare the performance of things.
exampleSentence: The new server is twice as fast as our old benchmark.

definition: Including people from different departments or skills.
exampleSentence: A cross-functional team of designers, developers and testers built the app.

definition: Working in short cycles and changing plans easily.
exampleSentence: Our company uses agile methods to deliver software in small steps.

definition: Needing attention quickly because it will soon be too late.
exampleSentence: This request is time-sensitive, so please answer before noon.

definition: Very important and needing to be done first.
exampleSentence: Security bugs are always high-priority tasks for our team.

definition: Happening one immediately after another.
exampleSentence: I have back-to-back meetings all afternoon, so I cannot call you.

definition: To change the rules or goals after work has started.
exampleSentence: It is unfair to move the goalposts when the project is almost finished.

definition: To increase the speed or amount of something.
exampleSentence: We need to ramp up production before the holiday season.

definition: When a project slowly grows beyond its original plan.
exampleSentence: Scope creep is the main reason our projects finish late.

definition: To start being used by real users.
exampleSentence: The new website will go live on Monday morning.
